request.tone: hopeful exploration adventure with tides, heights and a lost mapmaker; scariness and peril moderate
request.note: catalog book; plan written by reading the book

pitch.hero: Wren, a young mapmaker landed alone on an island no map has named
pitch.want: to fill one blank sheet with a true chart before dusk and win the Chart House apprenticeship
pitch.obstacle: tides, caves, heights and wonders that eat the day; only the summit shows the whole island
pitch.stake: the apprenticeship, and the lost mapmaker Alder's unfinished chart and wish
pitch.ending_kind: Alder's chart finished and named from the summit, a rescue or partial win, or a costly discovery

wren.name: Wren
wren.role: protagonist; a Chart House-trained would-be apprentice
wren.want: to chart the whole island truly before dusk and earn the apprenticeship
wren.voice: close third, past tense, no pronouns; careful, curious, tempted to linger over wonders

mate.name: the mate
mate.role: the ship's mate who sets the test and judges the chart
mate.want: a true chart drawn with Wren's own eyes
mate.voice: plain, weathered, sparing; pronounces short verdicts

alder.name: Alder
alder.role: the lost mapmaker who began the island's chart; absent, present through marks and notes
alder.want: for whoever comes after to finish the chart and name the island
alder.voice: a small, sure hand; warm, plain notes to a stranger

keepers.name: the Chart House keepers
keepers.role: the guild's elders who judge what mapmakers bring home
keepers.want: unstated; they fall silent before truly old maps
keepers.voice: no lines; a hush and leaning close

truth.question: How can Wren chart the whole unnamed island before dusk?
truth.statement: The island has never been named. Long ago the mapmaker Alder charted half of it, left that half chart at the ridge camp for whoever came after, and never came home after a storm took the boat. Marks, notes and messages all over the island point uphill to the camp. Wren wins by reaching it, carrying Alder's chart to the summit where the whole island can be seen, and finishing a true chart before the ship returns at dusk, as Alder wished.

wren_landed.text: Wren was landed alone by rowboat at first light on an island shore that no map had ever named.

wren_kit.text: Wren carries a satchel, a flask, a sketchbook for field notes, and one blank sheet of paper.

chart_test.text: To win the apprenticeship at the Chart House, Wren must fill the blank sheet with a true chart of the island before dusk.

ship_returns_dusk.text: The ship that brought Wren will return for Wren at dusk.

mate_set_rule.text: The ship's mate set the rule of the test.

chart_house_taught.text: Wren has been taught the mapmaker's craft by the Chart House.

five_ways.text: Five ways lead inland: the mangrove coast, the cloud-forest ridge, the sink-hole caverns, the ruined survey tower, and the tidal flats.

alder_named.text: Someone named Alder left marks on the island long before Wren came.

alder_mapmaker.text: Alder was a mapmaker who surveyed the island before Wren.

alder_camp.text: Alder had a camp up on the island's ridge.

alder_chart_at_camp.text: Alder left a chart of the island at the ridge camp for whoever came after.

alder_storm.text: A great storm came while Alder was working the island, and Alder meant to come back after it.

alder_lost.text: Alder never came home: a storm took the boat and the ship came too late.

alder_family.text: Alder left a family ashore; a child drew Alder a picture of a house and three figures holding hands.

alder_wish_finish.text: Alder asked that whoever came after finish the chart of the island.

alder_wish_name.text: Alder wished that whoever finished the chart would give the island its name.

alder_many_islands.text: Alder drew and signed charts of a dozen other islands in a long life of mapmaking.

alder_kind_note.text: In a tin in the cove's sea cave Alder left a spare pencil and a note: the way up is behind you, friend.

alder_strongbox.text: Under a floor slab of the tower ground room sits a locked iron strongbox with a rusted key on a nail.

alder_letter.text: The strongbox holds Alder's brass drawing tools and a sealed letter addressed to whoever finishes Alder's work.

alder_letter_text.text: Alder's letter charges the finisher to love the island, finish the map, and mind only the truth, not the glory.

alder_journal.text: Alder's journal, in the tin trunk at the camp, stops mid-sentence on the day a storm took the boat that never came back.

alder_journal_story.text: Alder's journal tells of mapping the island alone for seasons, naming a hidden cove, and waiting on the ridge for a ship that came too late.

alder_logbook.text: Alder's logbook in the tower says the true chart was carried to the ridge camp before a great storm, then stops.

alder_draft.text: A leather tube in the tower cellar holds Alder's abandoned, water-stained draft chart, with a safe path to the ridge sketched on it.

alder_bottle_msg.text: A corked bottle on the strand holds Alder's message: the island is real and worth naming, and its chart waits at the ridge camp.

alder_fuel_note.text: Inside the beacon fuel store Alder wrote: gone to finish the ridge chart, back by the storm.

alder_dial.text: Alder carved a stone compass dial on the headland with the bearing and name of every landmark on the coast.

alder_stake.text: A survey stake with a faded number and Alder's name stands in the otters' driftwood dam.

alder_gauge.text: Alder set a notched water gauge stone in the pool below the waterfall.

alder_blind.text: Alder's watching blind on the heron island has a tide table and headland bearings carved into its rails.

alder_boundary.text: A capstone in the meadow's tumbled cairn carries Alder's survey mark fixing the middle of the island.

alder_treetop.text: A treetop lookout in the grove has a brass sighting ring stamped with Alder's name.

alder_bench.text: Alder's name is carved among other mapmakers' marks on a mossy bench in the hidden dell.

alder_driftwood_msg.text: The carved driftwood holds Alder's name and a promise that a chart of the island was left at a camp on the ridge.

driftwood_marks.text: Carved driftwood on the log bridge bears old mapmaker's arrows: one toward the sea caves, one up toward high ground.

overhang_alder.text: Under a mossy overhang an old firepit, a tin cup and the scratched word Alder mark a shelter, with an arrow uphill to a camp.

alder_field_notes.text: Alder's field notes say Alder began a chart of the island and left it safe at a camp on the ridge.

tin_box.text: A moss-furred tin box marked with a compass rose is hidden in a cleft behind the orchids, holding papers, a pencil stub and a brass locket.

locket_girl.text: The brass locket holds a faded picture of a young girl who looks a little like Wren.

locket_held.text: Wren carries the brass locket from the tin box.

caverns_flood.text: The caverns below flood fast and deep at high tide.

cave_tide_line.text: A scratched line on the cave wall marks how high the water rises at the turn of the tide.

mangrove_ways.text: In the mangroves a log bridge lies upcoast, oyster rocks downcoast, a hidden creek inland, and a still green lagoon nearby.

log_bridge.text: A slippery fallen log bridges a mangrove channel where the tide is turning.

hidden_creek.text: A hidden creek runs inland from the mangrove coast.

hidden_cove.text: A hidden cove of calm water lies ringed by cliffs inside the reef.

reef_offshore.text: A long reef curls offshore around the island.

spring_above.text: Fresh water on the island comes down from a spring on higher ground.

island_spring.text: The island's spring is a cold clear pool that feeds every stream on the island.

ridge_camp_seen.text: A speck of grey canvas, a camp, stands high on the island's ridge.

camp_cairns.text: A line of small cairns marks the safe way up through broken rock toward the ridge camp.

summit_cairns.text: A line of cairns marks the safe way along the narrow path from the camp to the summit, beside a scree shortcut.

first_people.text: People found the island long before any mapmaker: the island's first people.

ochre_map.text: Red ochre handprints in the crystal cave form the oldest map of the island, marking the spring and the high peak.

star_map.text: A tilted slab on the cove path is pecked with a star map by which the first people steered toward the island's peak.

fishing_camp.text: A vanished fishing camp of stone drying racks and house posts lies on cleared ground across the lagoon.

grove_shrine.text: A shell-dressed cairn shrine topped by a carved wooden bird stands among the roots of the ancient grove.

stone_footprints.text: Children's footprints turned to stone lie on a pale beach beside the underground lake.

sandbar_wreck.text: An old wreck lies on a distant sandbar far out on the tidal flats.

marigold.text: The wreck on the bar is the Marigold, the ship that carried settler families to the island long ago.

flats_tide_rule.text: On the flats the returning tide comes in faster than a person can run.

cave_passages.text: From the cavern below the sink-hole, passages lead toward dripping water, a glitter, and warm breathing air, with a daylight hole above.

sinkhole_rope.text: A knotted rope tied to a root hangs down the sink-hole into the caves.

bat_colony.text: A colony of bats warms one passage of the caves.

searcher_lantern.text: A rusted lantern by goat bones in the stone gallery shows a searcher came that way before.

pale_gleam.text: Something pale gleams in a mossy hollow on the cloud-forest slope.

cove_compass_rose.text: An old compass rose drawn on a rock in the cove points up toward the ridge.

tower_built.text: The survey tower on the headland was built by mapmakers before Wren was born.

tower_logbook.text: A damp, swollen logbook lies on the slate desk in the tower's ground room.

tower_keeper_room.text: The tower's keeper's quarters hold a bunk, a cold hearth, a latched sea chest, and a wall of pinned charts.

beacon_dial.text: On the headland stand an old beacon brazier and a carved stone bearing dial.

brightness_uphill.text: A patch of brightness shows uphill through the mangrove trees, promising open ground.

reed_raft.text: Wren poled across to the heron island on a raft of lashed reeds.

fallen_chick.text: Wren set a fallen heron chick back on a low branch beneath its parents.

gully_tide_lines.text: Weed lines on the gully walls, above head height, show how deep and fast the gully floods.

far_shore.text: The wild windward far shore of cliffs, sea stacks and reef has never been mapped by anyone.

oyster_turtle.text: A small sea turtle lies stranded on its back in a draining pool among the oyster rocks.

cave_pup.text: A seal pup is stranded on a ledge in the warm bat cave, having come in through a flooded tube from the sea.

tangled_pup.text: A seal pup in the basking colony has one flipper snarled in old fishing net.

reef_turtle.text: From the summit, through the spyglass, Wren spots a small turtle on its back in a draining pool on the reef.

cove_pup.text: A young seal pup is trapped in a sea cave in the cove cliffs and cannot climb back out.

ship_can_be_signalled.text: From a high place the ship can be signalled to send grown hands to help.

alidade.text: Among the tower's ruined instruments is a working brass alidade for fixing distant points.

alidade_held.text: Wren carries the brass alidade from the tower.

tower_find_held.text: Wren carries a find from the survey tower.

rope_oil_held.text: Wren carries rope and a tin of oil from the tower cellar.

compass_held.text: Wren carries the brass pocket compass from the sea chest.

alder_pencil_held.text: Wren carries Alder's spare pencil from the cove sea cave.

letter_tools_held.text: Wren carries Alder's brass drawing tools and sealed letter from the strongbox.

alder_table_tools.text: On Alder's camp table lie pens, a brass spyglass and a small signal mirror, set out as if for the next mapmaker.

tin_trunk.text: A closed tin trunk sits under the cot in Alder's camp.

alder_chart_half.text: Alder's chart at the camp has half the island drawn in a fine sure hand and the rest left open.

alder_chart_detail.text: Alder's chart shows the coast, the caves, the reef and the cove; the high ground and the far shore are blank.

camp_tools_held.text: Wren carries Alder's camp tools: the pens and the brass spyglass.

banner_blank.text: Alder left the banner across the top of the half chart empty, as if the naming were meant for the finisher.

chart_signed.text: Wren has signed the finished chart.

summit_whole_view.text: From the summit cairn the whole island can be seen at once.

ship_back_early.text: The ship is already back, a far white speck standing off the reef.

distress_rhythm.text: Every Chart House apprentice is drilled in the flash, pause, flash distress rhythm.

ship_answers.text: The ship comes about and steers for the sheltered cove in answer to Wren's signal.

sailors_land.text: The mate sends two sailors ashore in the ship's boat to the cove.

chart_house_keepers.text: The Chart House has keepers who gather to judge the pages mapmakers bring home.

chart_unfinished.text: Wren ends the day with the island's chart left unfinished.

chart_complete.text: Wren ends the day with a complete, true chart of the whole island.

apprenticeship_won.text: The mate gives Wren the apprenticeship at the Chart House.

apprenticeship_not_won.text: Wren does not win the apprenticeship this day.

island_named_alder.text: Wren names the island Alder's Island.

island_named_both.text: Wren names the island for both mapmakers together.

island_name_left.text: Wren leaves the banner blank for the Chart House to name the island.

two_charts.text: Wren makes two finished copies of the chart, a master and a working copy.

next_island_honour.text: The mate gives Wren the honour of naming the next island the Chart House sends a mapmaker to find.

safe_landing_chart.text: Wren charts the reef, the cove and the safe channels for ships to land.

far_shore_charted.text: Wren charts the never-mapped far shore from the summit.

oyster_turtle_righted.text: Wren rights the stranded turtle among the oyster rocks and it swims away.

tangled_pup_freed.text: Wren frees the tangled seal pup, and the colony flees into the sea.

cove_pup_rescued.text: Wren and the sailors lift the seal pup out of the cove sea cave and free it.

reef_turtle_rescued.text: Wren and the sailors carry the reef turtle to deep water and free it.

driftwood_carving.text: A knot of driftwood wedged against the log bridge is carved with old, deliberate marks.

seep_inland.text: A clear seep climbs inland out of the marsh toward a spring.

n_open.event: Wren is rowed ashore at first light with a blank sheet and told to chart the island before the ship returns at dusk.

n_start.event: Five ways lead inland from the beach and Wren weighs them.

mg_enter.event: Wren wades into the mangroves at low water and sees four ways: log bridge, oyster rocks, hidden creek, lagoon.

mg_bridge.event: Halfway across the slippery log Wren spots carved driftwood as the tide rises.

mg_carve.event: The carving is mapmaker's shorthand with arrows to the sea caves and to high ground.

mg_readmarks.event: The message is signed Alder and promises a chart left at a camp on the ridge.

mg_farbank.event: Herons burst up on the far bank and the path splits between a mud slick and firm palms.

e_mg_mud_trap.event: Wren sinks in the mud slick; the tide covers the log bridge and that coast is cut off.

mg_highground.event: Wren climbs out of the swamp and sees the reef and a hidden cove; a goat track forks to the cove or a spring gully.

mg_oyster.event: Among the oyster rocks a small turtle lies stranded on its back in a draining pool.

mg_turtle_note.event: Wren weighs righting the turtle now against marking it and signalling the ship for help later.

e_mg_turtle_seen.event: Wren rights the turtle; the tide returns and only one honest corner of reef gets mapped.

mg_rockpath.event: A cold sweet seep threads inland, a guide up toward a spring on higher ground.

mg_seep.event: Wren fills the flask in a fern gully that forks to a bright spring pool or a mossy overhang.

mg_overhang.event: Under the overhang are an old firepit, a tin cup, and Alder's name with an arrow uphill to a camp.

e_mg_shelter.event: Wren sketches the snug shelter while the morning slips away; only that corner is drawn.

mg_creek.event: On the hidden creek Wren meets otters; the ways go upstream, into the trees, or to a loud heron island.

mg_otter.event: A gravel bar and sweet fresh water show a spring higher up, and Wren follows it.

mg_trees.event: Without the creek Wren must choose between a brightness uphill and a level game trail.

mg_gametrail.event: The game trail curls back on itself; Wren may turn back toward the brightness or gamble on.

e_mg_lost.event: The trail was a loop; an hour is wasted and the coast is guessed with its middle blank.

cf_enter.event: Wren climbs into misty forest where a switchback, a traverse, a pale gleam and a waterfall roar offer ways up.

cf_switch.event: On a ledge the switchback splits into a bare rock rib and a green shelf.

cf_ledge.event: Wren climbs the airy rib to a grassy bench and a worn ridge path.

cf_shelf.event: The shelf is a surveyor's contour path that brings Wren to the grassy bench.

cf_bench.event: On the windy bench a trail climbs toward a grey canvas camp, and an ancient grove stands aside.

cf_campapproach.event: A line of careful cairns guides Wren through broken rock toward the camp.

camp_ascent1.event: On the open, windy ridge Wren follows the cairns toward the distant camp.

camp_ascent2.event: The ridge splits into a sheltered ledge and an airy crest, and the height daunts Wren.

e_ascent_daunted.event: Vertigo freezes Wren on the ridge; Wren edges back and maps it from below, the camp out of reach.

camp_ascent3a.event: The sheltered ledge, set with alpine flowers, climbs back to the crest.

camp_ascent3b.event: Wren crosses the spine of the island in streaming cloud and comes down to a level shelf.

camp_ascent4.event: The two ways rejoin on a shelf thick with cairns, one short climb below the camp.

camp_ascent5.event: At the end of the cairns stands a grey canvas camp with Alder's name on a board over the door.

cf_traverse.event: Tracing a stream upward, Wren finds the island's spring; a deer path leads off to a hidden dell.

cf_upper.event: Higher up, a faint path climbs to the ridge while the pale gleam shows in the hollow below.

cf_hollow.event: The gleam is white orchids hiding a moss-furred tin box marked with a compass rose.

cf_box.event: The box holds field notes, a pencil stub, and a locket with a girl who looks a little like Wren.

e_cf_locket.event: Wren pockets the locket and maps the ridge in a distracted scrawl, the mystery carried home.

cf_notes.event: Alder's notes tell of a chart left at the ridge camp and warn that the caverns flood at high tide.

cv_enter.event: Wren climbs down an old knotted rope into a cavern with three passages and a skylight.

cv_water.event: An underground stream bears a scratched tide line; it leads to an arch, upstream, or a glowworm rift.

cv_arch.event: At the low arch the tide is rising; a dry ledge leads to light, the arch is a shortcut.

e_cv_flood.event: The passage floods as the tide line warned; Wren scrambles back and the caves stay a blank.

cv_upflow.event: Upstream, a shaft of daylight falls into the chamber where the island's spring wells up.

cv_glitter.event: Quartz veins glitter around red ochre handprints left long before any mapmaker.

cv_ochre.event: The handprints form the oldest map of the island, marking the spring and the peak.

e_cv_paintings.event: Wren copies the ochre map in full; the keepers fall silent over it, but the island above is half drawn.

cv_deepglow.event: Wren squeezes out into a hidden cove inside the reef; a dark branch leads to lapping water.

cv_warm.event: In the warm passage bats roost above a seal pup stranded on a ledge.

cv_pup.event: The pup came through a flooded tube; Wren can mark it and signal the ship or try alone.

e_cv_pup_fail.event: The pup is too heavy; Wren marks the sea tube for help and backs away.

cv_backout.event: Leaving the bat cave, Wren finds a root-choked vent onto the high slope.

cv_tohigh.event: Wren comes up on the ridge flank with the island below and a camp in sight above.

tw_enter.event: The leaning survey tower, built by mapmakers before Wren was born, offers a ground room, a stair, a cellar, and quarters.

tw_ground.event: Among ruined instruments lie a swollen logbook and a loose floor slab.

e_tw_log.event: The logbook is Alder's: the chart went to the ridge camp before a storm; reading it takes the day.

tw_salvage.event: Wren finds a working brass alidade for fixing points from a height.

tw_toridge.event: Carrying the tower's find, Wren follows the headland path to a camp seen on the ridge.

tw_stair.event: Two thirds up the stair a span has fallen; a bold stride or a crumbling ledge remains.

e_tw_stair_fail.event: The ledge crumbles; Wren retreats and that corner is drawn from guesswork.

tw_top.event: From the top Wren sees the island's shape, a hidden cove, and a camp below the summit.

tw_ridgeway.event: Wren walks a knife of rock from the tower to the bench where the camp trail begins.

tw_cellar.event: The cellar holds rope, oil, a lamp, and a leather chart tube.

tw_tube.event: The tube holds Alder's ruined draft; the good copy went to the ridge camp, and the safe path is sketched.

e_tw_draft.event: Wren copies Alder's draft faithfully and ends with someone else's half map.

tw_supplies.event: With rope and oil, Wren follows a chalk line toward a camp on the ridge.

tf_enter.event: Wren steps onto the flats, remembering the tide rule; a wrecked sandbar, channels, a strand and mussel beds wait.

tf_sandbar.event: The wreck on the bar is a beautiful subject, but the tide has turned.

e_tf_stranded.event: The tide cuts Wren off; Wren wades back chest-deep and loses the day drying out.

tf_sketchrun.event: Wren sketches the wreck and reaches firm ground just in time; a green gap leads inland.

tf_gap.event: A stream valley climbs inland toward falling water and the island's source.

tf_channel.event: The firm channels lead to a cliff gap, up a firm rise, or out to the great wreck on the bar.

tf_cliffgap.event: Through a low-tide gap in the cliffs Wren enters a hidden cove.

tf_strand.event: Along the strand line lies a corked bottle with a paper inside.

tf_bottle.event: The bottle holds Alder's message: the island is worth naming and its chart waits at the ridge camp.

e_tf_bottle.event: Wren goes back to wait for the ship with Alder's note but no chart; the apprenticeship must wait.

L_cove.event: Wren reaches the hidden cove with a fresh rill, a hand-cut path, a compass rose, and tide pools.

e_cove_rest.event: The calm lulls Wren; only the cove gets drawn.

cove_rise.event: Partway up the hand-cut path a tilted slab is pecked with patterned dots.

cove_starrock.event: The dots are a star map the first people steered by toward the island's peak.

e_star_map.event: Wren copies the star map in full; the keepers lean close, but the coast stays unfinished.

cove_ridge.event: The path tops out on the windy bench, with a camp in sight up the ridge.

L_fresh.event: At the island's spring Wren sees how the water runs to five shores and a camp shows up the ridge.

e_fresh_linger.event: The streams branch without end; Wren ends with a tangle of blue lines and no coast.

fresh_study.event: Wren sketches the island's whole drainage as a frame for the chart.

fresh_climb.event: The path climbs to a high meadow with goats and the camp trail beyond.

fresh_meadow.event: An old tumbled boundary cairn stands in the meadow by the camp trail.

fresh_cairn.event: The cairn's capstone carries Alder's mark fixing the middle of the island.

e_fresh_cairn.event: Wren copies the mark, dozes in the meadow, and goes down with only half a chart.

L_camp.event: Alder's empty camp holds a half-drawn chart, pens, a spyglass, a signal mirror, and a trunk under the cot.

camp_chart.event: Alder's chart has the coast drawn and the high ground blank, with a note: finish this, and it is yours.

e_camp_copy.event: Wren brings down a copy of Alder's half chart; the mate says a copy is a story, not a survey.

camp_trunk.event: The trunk holds spare nibs, ink, and Alder's journal, which stops on the day a storm took the boat.

camp_journal.event: The journal tells Alder's story and ends with a wish: finish the chart and give the island its name.

e_camp_journal.event: Wren spends the afternoon on Alder's journal and goes home with a blank chart and Alder's story.

camp_ready.event: With tools in hand and Alder's half chart under one arm, Wren sets out for the summit.

camp_summitpath.event: With chart and tools carried safe, Wren reaches a narrow path where cairns mark the safe way beside a scree shortcut.

e_camp_scree.event: The scree slides away; shaken, Wren judges the summit too far and the high chart stays unfinished.

ridge_notch.event: The cairns lead through a wind-funnelling notch to a final boulder field.

wind_gap.event: Block by block Wren crosses the boulders to the summit's foot.

L_summit.event: From the summit cairn Wren sees the whole island at once, with the wind fierce and the light turning.

e_summit_gaze.event: Wren stares at the view until the light turns and draws none of it.

summit_survey.event: On the summit Wren fills Alder's blank half fast, then must choose what to fix first.

e_ch_rush.event: Wren rushes everything and the chart comes out full but wrong; the mate calls it a near miss.

ch_sightings.event: With Alder's spyglass Wren fixes every distant point and the island's shape tightens.

ch_reef.event: Wren fixes the reef, cove and channels Alder had begun into a safe-landing chart.

e_ch_reef.event: The mate calls Wren's safe-landing chart the map that keeps sailors alive and takes Wren on.

ch_gather.event: In the lee of the cairn Wren lays Alder's chart beside the day's sketches, ready to draw.

ch_table.event: Wren must choose how to draw the chart: bold ink, fine pencil, or two copies.

ch_ink.event: With Alder's good pen Wren inks one seamless island from Alder's half and Wren's.

ch_pencil.event: Wren pencils every pool and stream as the light nearly goes.

e_ch_dusk.event: Wren keeps adding detail until the ship's horn sounds; the chart is lovely and never finished.

ch_double.event: Wren draws two true charts of Alder's island, a master and a working copy.

ch_sign.event: Alder left the chart's banner empty for the finisher, and Wren must choose a name or a signature.

e_ch_alder_name.event: Wren names the island Alder's Island; the mate understands the promise kept and takes Wren on.

e_ch_both_name.event: Wren names both mapmakers on the banner; the mate calls it the finest first survey in years.

e_ch_survey.event: Wren signs the survey and leaves the name to the House; the mate finds no fault and offers the place.

ch_sign_double.event: At the boat Wren chooses whether to hand over both charts or keep the spare.

e_ch_double_win.event: Wren hands over both charts; the mate praises the judgement and takes Wren on.

e_ch_spare.event: Wren gives one chart, keeps the spare, and is welcomed to the Chart House.

summit_signal.event: The ship is back off the reef; Wren could flash Alder's mirror to call the boat in for a stranded turtle.

signal_aim.event: Wren catches the low sun on the little mirror and holds the beam on the far sail.

signal_flash.event: Wren works the old distress rhythm for a long while with no answer.

ship_turns.event: The ship comes about for the cove, called by a lost mapmaker's mirror.

race_down.event: Wren pockets the mirror and runs cairn to cairn past the camp toward the cove as the boat comes in.

meet_boat.event: Two sailors land; the turtle still lies on the reef, and Wren heard a seal pup crying in a sea cave.

e_rescue_pup.event: Wren and the sailors free the seal pup; the mate says a mapmaker who saves a life is worth keeping.

e_rescue_turtle.event: Wren and the sailors free the turtle; the chart is half finished, but the mate offers the place.

mg_lagoon.event: At the lagoon wait a half-sunk dugout canoe, a root tunnel, and a driftwood dam.

mg_canoe.event: The old dugout may be sound or may sink; it can be tested with care or trusted recklessly.

e_mg_canoe.event: The dugout swamps; the sketchbook is saved but the morning and that coast are lost.

mg_paddle.event: From the water the shore traces easily, and Wren spots a strip of cleared ground.

mg_lagfar.event: The cleared ground holds a stone mound and posts; a firm path climbs toward the creek.

mg_ruin.event: The stones are a vanished fishing camp of people who lived on the island long before any chart.

e_mg_village.event: Wren maps the vanished camp in loving detail and brings home a village instead of a coastline.

mg_lagtunnel.event: The root tunnel forks toward open sky or deeper into the dark.

e_mg_tunnellost.event: The tunnel branches endlessly; Wren backtracks by feel and leaves it a rough scribble.

mg_dam.event: In the otters' dam stands a survey stake burned with a number and the name Alder.

e_mg_stake.event: Wren carries Alder's stake home like treasure and barely starts the map.

cf_falls.event: At the waterfall Wren can climb the wet rocks, cross a log above the lip, or wade the pool.

cf_fallclimb.event: The wet rocks have good holds for a careful climber and danger for a reckless one.

e_cf_slip.event: A hold peels away and Wren slides into the pool; the ridge stays unmapped.

cf_fallcross.event: The log holds and Wren crosses to the upper traverse.

cf_fallpool.event: In the pool lies a notched water gauge stone carved with Alder's name.

e_cf_gauge.event: Wren copies Alder's gauge notch by notch and leaves the coast for a quicker day.

cv_skylight.event: Under the skylight a rock slope climbs to daylight, and a gallery of formations glows aside.

cv_chimney.event: The way out is a chimney climb that needs a steady pace.

e_cv_chimney.event: Wren tires halfway, slides back down safely, and must find another way.

cv_gallery.event: In the stone gallery lie goat bones and a rusted lantern from an earlier searcher.

e_cv_lantern.event: Wren draws the stone gallery and its lantern; the island above stays undrawn.

tw_quarters.event: The keeper's quarters hold a bunk, a cold hearth, a sea chest, and a wall of charts.

tw_wallcharts.event: The wall holds a dozen other islands, all drawn and signed by Alder.

e_tw_charts.event: Wren studies Alder's lifetime of charts and rows home with this island still blank.

tw_seachest.event: The sea chest holds an oilskin, a working compass, and a child's drawing made for Alder.

e_tw_drawing.event: The drawing of a family who waited undoes Wren; the morning goes and the chart stays bare.

tf_mussel.event: Past the mussel beds are basking seals and a deep gully toward the cliffs.

tf_seals.event: A seal pup is caught in old net; freeing it might stampede the colony.

e_tf_seals.event: Wren frees the pup; the colony flees and the tide window closes on half-drawn flats.

tf_gully.event: Weed lines above head height show how fast the gully floods.

e_tf_gully.event: Wren lingers, the gully floods, and the shortcut is lost to the sea.

ch_farshore.event: Through the glass Wren charts the wild far shore no one had ever mapped.

e_ch_farshore.event: Wren brings down the never-mapped far shore with the rest only sketched; the mate keeps Wren on.

ch_seal_final.event: With the masterwork drawn and signed, Wren can hand it over or ring its margins with the island's life.

e_ch_living.event: Wren's living chart wins the apprenticeship and the honour of naming the next island.

e_ch_clean.event: The mate finds no fault in the clean chart and takes Wren on as the newest apprentice.

mg_heron.event: Wren poles a reed raft to the heron island: a watching blind, a mud bank, and the rookery.

mg_blind.event: The blind is Alder's, carved with a tide table and headland bearings; a plank walk leads to the seep.

e_mg_tidetable.event: Wren copies Alder's whole tide table and leaves the island's shape for another day.

mg_mudbank.event: A firm sand ribbon crosses the soft mud bank toward the far channel.

e_mg_birdstorm.event: Wren startles the flock, sinks in the mud, and the heron island becomes a smudge.

mg_farchannel.event: Wren crosses the far channel dry-shod and heads for a lookout rise.

mg_rookery.event: Wren returns a fallen chick to its branch and sketches the colony.

e_mg_chick.event: Wren watches the herons too long; the rookery is drawn and the coast is not.

cf_grove.event: In an ancient grove hang a frayed rope ladder and a small shell-dressed cairn shrine.

cf_canopy.event: The lower rungs hold, but the upper rungs look rotten.

e_cf_ladder.event: A rotten rung snaps; Wren climbs down shaking and the grove is drawn from the ground.

cf_treetop.event: The platform is a lookout with a brass sighting ring stamped Alder, and the whole ridge to the sea is in view.

e_cf_canopy.event: Wren lingers in the treetops and climbs down with a lovely fragment and no chart.

cf_shrine.event: The shrine, topped with a carved wooden bird, was left by the island's first people.

e_cf_shrine.event: The grove's hush holds Wren; only the shrine is drawn.

cv_lake.event: A black underground lake has a plank raft on a pale beach.

cv_raft.event: The raft floats but its lashings need a slow, even crossing.

e_cv_raft.event: A lashing snaps and Wren is dunked; the crossing ends before it begins.

cv_farcave.event: On the far shore blind white fish hang in the water and a flowstone stair climbs to daylight.

e_cv_fish.event: Wren fills pages with blind fish and leaves the island blank.

cv_lakebeach.event: The pale beach holds children's footprints turned to stone.

e_cv_prints.event: Wren maps every stone footprint and climbs out with the island nearly blank.

tw_beacon.event: On the headland stand an old iron beacon brazier and a carved stone bearing dial.

tw_brazier.event: The dead beacon once warned ships off the reef; its fuel store must be nearby.

e_tw_nofuel.event: Wren gives up on the dead beacon, an hour wasted on a dead end.

tw_fuelstore.event: Inside the fuel store Alder wrote: gone to finish the ridge chart, back by the storm.

e_tw_note.event: Wren sits with Alder's last message all morning and goes home with it instead of a chart.

tw_viewdial.event: The dial is Alder's stone compass rose, naming every landmark in sight.

e_tw_dial.event: Wren copies every bearing on Alder's dial; a frame, but no coastline.

tf_wreck.event: The great wreck has a flooded hold and a tilted deck up to a figurehead.

tf_hold.event: Cargo shows in the green water, but the tide is starting back.

e_tf_hold.event: Wren is nearly trapped in the wreck and escapes soaked, the flats unfinished.

tf_cargo.event: A green bell names the wreck the Marigold, the ship that brought settler families to the island.

e_tf_bell.event: Wren pieces together the Marigold's ending and the flats become a soaking blur.

tf_deck.event: From the high bow the whole pattern of the flats is laid out below.

e_tf_figurehead.event: Wren draws the figurehead lovingly and only just beats the tide, the coast still bare.

cove_pools.event: Tide pools ring the cove and a low sea cave breathes with the swell.

cove_seacave.event: In the cave Alder left a pencil and a note: the way up is behind you, friend.

e_cove_tin.event: Wren is moved by Alder's kindness and climbs out with a full heart and an empty page.

cove_rockpool.event: The pools trace the reef edge and the cove's safe channel.

e_cove_reefmap.event: Wren maps the reef pools perfectly and leaves the island blank above.

cv_rift.event: A glowworm rift leads to a narrow squeeze or a still pool.

cv_squeeze.event: The squeeze will pass with a calm wriggle but not a panicked rush.

e_cv_squeeze.event: Wren sticks fast, calms down, wriggles back, and leaves the rift as a shaky note.

cv_glowworm.event: Wren draws the rift by glowworm light and hears a spring ahead.

e_cv_glow.event: Wren loses the afternoon under the glowworms and goes home with an underground sky.

cf_dell.event: A sheltered dell holds a small spring, a carved bench, and a soft lawn for resting.

e_cf_dell_lost.event: Wren dozes for an hour; only the dell is drawn.

cf_dellspring.event: The dell's stream gathers others and leads to the island's spring, the heart of its water.

cf_dellcarve.event: The bench is carved with generations of mapmakers' marks, Alder's name among them.

e_cf_carve.event: Wren copies every mapmaker's mark on the bench while the island stays bare.

tw_slab.event: Under the slab is a rusted strongbox with a key on a nail.

e_tw_slab.event: Forcing the lock bends the bar and grazes a knuckle; the box stays shut.

tw_cache.event: The strongbox holds brass drawing tools and a sealed letter from Alder to whoever finishes the work.

e_tw_cache.event: Alder's letter charges the finisher to love the island and finish the map; reading it takes the light.

tf_dune.event: A marker post tops the dunes, but soft sand makes the climb exhausting.

e_tf_dune.event: Wren flounders in the dunes and gives up; the flats become a scribble.

tf_marker.event: From the surveyor's marker post the whole pattern of the flats lies open.

e_tf_marker.event: Wren perfects a map of the flats from the dune and leaves the rest untouched.

e_mg_mud_trap.gift: the mud slick shows that a quick way across soft ground can cost the whole coast

e_mg_turtle_seen.gift: a kindness done well and one honest corner of reef, traded for the rest of the island

e_mg_shelter.gift: Alder's snug shelter, and the lesson that comfort quietly eats a mapmaker's morning

e_mg_lost.gift: the mangrove's loop teaches that a map you cannot see is no map at all

e_ascent_daunted.gift: turning back on a dizzy ridge is not cowardice; the high camp waits for a braver day

e_cf_locket.gift: the mystery of a girl in a locket who looks a little like Wren

e_cv_flood.gift: the scratched tide line was a true warning; the caves become a question mark

e_cv_paintings.gift: the oldest map of all, a hand-printed island that silences the Chart House keepers

e_cv_pup_fail.gift: some rescues need more than one pair of hands; the sea tube is marked for help

e_tw_log.gift: Alder's last logbook entry: the true chart went to the ridge camp before the storm

e_tw_stair_fail.gift: a crumbling ledge says no, and a wise climber listens

e_tw_draft.gift: a faithful copy of Alder's draft, and the lesson that copying is not looking

e_tf_stranded.gift: a cold lesson in how fast the tide fills the low channels

e_tf_bottle.gift: Alder's message from the sea, and the reminder that a tale is not a chart

e_cove_rest.gift: the calm cove drawn perfectly and the cost of lingering in a lovely place

e_star_map.gift: the first people's star map, a navigation older than any chart

e_fresh_linger.gift: a beautiful tangle of streams with no coast to hold it

e_fresh_cairn.gift: Alder's boundary mark fixing the island's middle, and a nap that costs the edges

e_camp_copy.gift: the mate's verdict that a copied map is a story, not a survey

e_camp_journal.gift: Alder's whole story and the wish to finish and name the island, kept from fading

e_camp_scree.gift: the cairns were right; some shortcuts are only the long way to a fall

e_summit_gaze.gift: the whole island seen at once, and drawn not at all

e_ch_rush.gift: a near miss: the seeing was there and only the patience failed

e_ch_reef.gift: the chart that keeps sailors alive, and the apprenticeship it wins

e_ch_dusk.gift: the loveliest never-finished map, and the lesson that done beats perfect

e_ch_alder_name.gift: Alder's Island named, Alder's promise kept, and the apprenticeship won

e_ch_both_name.gift: both mapmakers named together on one true chart; credit shared is worth training

e_ch_survey.gift: a flawless survey signed small, the name left to the House, the place offered on the spot

e_ch_double_win.gift: two true charts and the judgement to keep a spare, which wins the apprenticeship

e_ch_spare.gift: one chart given and one kept: the first sheet of Wren's own library

e_rescue_pup.gift: the seal pup freed by three pairs of hands; reading a coast well enough to save a life

e_rescue_turtle.gift: the turtle returned to deep water; a map used to help as well as to win

e_mg_canoe.gift: the swamped dugout shows the reckless way to trust old wood

e_mg_village.gift: the vanished fishing camp mapped stone by stone, a village instead of a coastline

e_mg_tunnellost.gift: under the roots some places keep their secrets, and a mapmaker learns to leave them

e_mg_stake.gift: Alder's survey stake carried home as a relic of the mapmaker who came first

e_cf_slip.gift: a moment of hurry on wet rock costs the ridge

e_cf_gauge.gift: Alder's water gauge copied notch by notch, a year of the falls understood

e_cv_chimney.gift: sliding back down before a slip becomes a fall is the right call

e_cv_lantern.gift: a frozen forest of stone and an earlier searcher's lantern, drawn in place of a chart

e_tw_charts.gift: Alder's lifetime of islands, an education worth more than a single test

e_tw_drawing.gift: the family Alder left ashore, a thing a mapmaker cannot draw

e_tf_seals.gift: a pup freed and the tide window paid for it

e_tf_gully.gift: forgetting the first rule of the flats in a flooding gully

e_ch_farshore.gift: the coast no one had ever mapped, and a mate who keeps the finder on

e_ch_living.gift: a chart that holds the island's life, the apprenticeship, and the right to name the next island

e_ch_clean.gift: a clean, faultless first survey, the kind the Chart House lives on

e_mg_tidetable.gift: Alder's carved tide table, a map of time rather than of land

e_mg_birdstorm.gift: a storm of wings shows why you keep to the firm ribbon

e_mg_chick.gift: a living page of herons and a chick set safe, with the coast left waiting

e_cf_ladder.gift: a ladder that cannot be trusted is a ladder to leave

e_cf_canopy.gift: a rare treetop view few people ever see, and the day it costs

e_cf_shrine.gift: the first people's shrine and the stillness of the grove carried home

e_cv_raft.gift: the black lake demands respect and a slow crossing

e_cv_fish.gift: eyeless white fish no chart had shown, a wonder but not a survey

e_cv_prints.gift: the stone footprints of children who walked the deep shore an age ago

e_tw_nofuel.gift: a dead end and the hard lesson of when to cut a loss

e_tw_note.gift: Alder's last message, back by the storm, carried home instead of a coastline

e_tw_dial.gift: Alder's stone compass copied whole, a frame with no picture inside

e_tf_hold.gift: a near trap in the wreck, and gladness to be standing on dry sand

e_tf_bell.gift: the Marigold's story, the settler ship that foundered a stone's throw from shore

e_tf_figurehead.gift: the ship's guardian drawn with love, a face remembered and a map unmade

e_cove_tin.gift: Alder's kind note to a stranger, a friend across the years

e_cove_reefmap.gift: a flawless reef edge a captain could steer by, and no middle

e_cv_squeeze.gift: the panic of a tight squeeze, and calm breathing that gets you out

e_cv_glow.gift: an underground sky of glowworms worth losing an afternoon beneath

e_cf_dell_lost.gift: the secret green room and the cost of a nap

e_cf_carve.gift: the long company of mapmakers carved in the bench, Alder among them

e_tw_slab.gift: some locks only open for patience

e_tw_cache.gift: Alder's letter, a blessing that makes Wren feel chosen

e_tf_dune.gift: a good idea that becomes a bad one in sliding sand

e_tf_marker.gift: the flats perfected from the dune, and the trap of perfecting a finished corner

notes: The book declares no variables, so the plan has no threads.
Choice labels that take an object (chart, tools, compass, pencil, alidade) record the possession as choice establishes.
